intro.title: Six stages, one accountable team
intro.text: No handovers between a designer who disappears and a contractor who improvises. The people who draw your space are the people who build it, and the same project manager owns the programme from survey to snag list.

stages.name: Listen
stages.title: Brief & site survey
stages.summary: A 60-minute consultation, a measured survey and an honest read on the building — including the things that will cost you money if ignored.

stages.name: Plan
stages.title: Concept & space planning
stages.summary: Layout options tested against how you actually use the space: circulation, daylight, storage, headcount and the view from the door.

stages.name: Design
stages.title: Design development
stages.summary: Materials, lighting and joinery resolved to specification. Every decision written down with a code, a supplier and a price attached.

stages.name: See
stages.title: 3D visualisation & approval
stages.summary: Photoreal views built from the same model the workshop uses, so the image you approve is the geometry we cut.

stages.name: Draw
stages.title: Construction & shop drawings
stages.summary: Coordinated MEP, reflected ceilings, partitions and full joinery shop drawings issued for manufacture — the set your landlord approves too.

stages.name: Build
stages.title: Manufacture, site & handover
stages.summary: Workshop production runs in parallel with site works. Friday photo reports, a resident supervisor, and a snag list closed before the final payment.

promises.title: One accountable team
promises.text: Design, workshop and site under a single contract and a single project manager.

promises.title: Fixed-price proposals
promises.text: A line-item BOQ taken from the drawings, so there is nowhere for an allowance to hide.

promises.title: Approved before production
promises.text: The 3D model and the workshop drawings are the same model. What you sign is what we cut.

promises.title: Friday, every Friday
promises.text: Photos, progress against programme, decisions needed next week, and risks we can see coming.
